name: manual_022af4
claim: When a CodeRabbit finding cites a language-agnostic coding-style guideline (e.g. '**/*: always create new objects, use immutable update patterns'), verify the pattern has a real non-degrading equivalent in the target language before applying it, rather than mechanically transferring it.

decisions.notes: orama PR #298 review 4890542470 flagged bash 'arr+=(...)' loop appends as violating the immutability guideline. Researched via Greg's Wiki BashFAQ/005: arr+=() is the documented, canonical append idiom since Bash 3.1 -- not a full-array-copy the way JS 'arr = [...arr, x]' is. Applying the JS/OOP-oriented rule literally would have made the code less idiomatic with no real benefit. Skipped with a researched reply rather than blind-applying or blind-ignoring.
